title: Filter ERROR Logs
description: Show all lines in app.log containing the string ERROR.
hint: Use the standard grep command without any flags: grep PATTERN FILE

title: Count Error Occurrences
description: Count how many ERROR lines exist in app.log. Output only the count.

title: Filter Multiple Levels with Extended Regex
description: Show all ERROR and WARN lines together from app.log.
hint: Use grep -E with the alternation operator | (pipe).

title: Invert Match to Exclude Info
description: Show all lines that are NOT INFO level in app.log.

title: Display Matches with Line Numbers
description: Show lines in app.log containing ERROR prefixed with their line numbers.
hint: Use the -n flag to prefix output with line numbers.

title: Count HTTP 500 Internal Server Errors
description: Count HTTP 500 errors in access.log. Ensure you match exact status code 500.

title: Identify Failed Logins
description: Find all failed login attempts (HTTP status 401) in access.log.

title: Clean Server Config (No Comments or Blanks)
description: Show only active configuration lines in server.conf (exclude lines starting with # and blank lines).
hint: Use grep -Ev '^#|^$' to exclude comment and empty lines.

title: Extract IP Addresses Only
description: Extract only the IP addresses from access.log.

title: Detect Web Probing Attacks
description: Find suspicious requests containing admin or wp- in access.log.

title: Case-Insensitive Database Search
description: Find all mentions of 'database' in app.log regardless of casing.

title: Error Search with Context
description: Show each ERROR line in app.log with 1 line of surrounding context before and after.

title: Find Bash Shell Users
description: List all user records in users.txt that have /bin/bash as their shell.

title: Identify Service Accounts (nologin)
description: Find all non-login service accounts in users.txt (containing nologin).

title: Count Attacker IP Requests
description: Count the total number of requests originating from IP 203.0.113.7 in access.log.

title: Substitute Port Number
description: Substitute port 8080 with port 9090 in server.conf (preview output without modifying original file).

title: Delete Comment Lines
description: Delete all lines starting with # from server.conf.
hint: Use the d command with address /^#/: sed '/^#/d' server.conf

title: Strip Comments and Blank Lines
description: Delete both comment lines and empty lines from server.conf in a single sed command.
hint: Chain delete commands with semicolon: sed '/^#/d; /^$/d' server.conf

title: Global Substitution of Log Level
description: Replace every occurrence of 'info' with 'debug' in server.conf.
hint: Use the g flag: sed 's/info/debug/g' server.conf

title: Print Specific Line Range
description: Print only lines 5 through 10 of app.log.
hint: Suppress automatic printing with -n and use 5,10p: sed -n '5,10p' app.log

title: Grep-Style Pattern Printing with Sed
description: Print only the ERROR lines from app.log using sed.

title: Replace Hostname with IP Address
description: Change 'localhost' to '127.0.0.1' in server.conf.

title: Wrap Warning Tags
description: Wrap all occurrences of WARN with *** WARN *** in app.log.

title: Extract Field by Stripping Suffix
description: Extract only the username (text before the first colon) from users.txt.
hint: Delete from the first colon to the end of line: sed 's/:.*//' users.txt

title: Custom Delimiters for Path Substitution
description: In users.txt, replace /bin/bash with /bin/sh without backslash clutter.
hint: Use pipe | as the delimiter: sed 's|/bin/bash|/bin/sh|g' users.txt

title: Early Termination with Quit Command
description: Show the first 5 lines of access.log using sed quit (5q).

title: Comment Out Configuration Lines
description: Add a '# ' comment marker before every line starting with 'port' in server.conf.

title: Squeeze Multiple Spaces
description: Normalise whitespace in server.conf by squeezing multiple spaces into a single space.

title: Back-Reference Format Inversion
description: Turn 'port 8080' into '8080 is the port' in server.conf using regex back-references.
hint: Use sed -E 's/port ([0-9]+)/\1 is the port/' server.conf

title: Print Leading Field ($1)
description: Print just the IP address (field 1) from every line of access.log.

title: Extract Multiple Discontiguous Fields
description: Print the HTTP status code (field 9) and byte size (field 10) from access.log separated by space.

title: Filter Lines by Field Condition
description: Print entire lines for requests in access.log that returned HTTP status 500.

title: Custom Delimiter Field Extraction
description: Print usernames (field 1) from the colon-separated users.txt file.

title: Extract Full Names from Passwd Format
description: Print the full name (field 5) of each user in users.txt.

title: Parse CSV and Skip Header Line
description: From employees.csv, print employee name (field 2) and salary (field 4), skipping the CSV header.
hint: Use -F, and condition NR > 1: awk -F, 'NR>1 {print $2, $4}' employees.csv

title: Calculate Total Sum Across File
description: Sum the total number of bytes served (field 10) across all requests in access.log and print the total in END.

title: Compute Average Salary Across All Staff
description: Calculate the average salary of all employees in employees.csv (skipping header).

title: Filtered Group Average Calculation
description: Find the average salary of the Engineering department only from employees.csv.

title: Group-by Count with Associative Arrays
description: Count how many requests each IP made in access.log, then sort descending by count.
hint: awk '{c[$1]++} END {for (ip in c) print c[ip], ip}' access.log | sort -rn
solution: awk "{c[\$1]++} END {for (ip in c) print c[ip], ip}" access.log | sort -rn

title: HTTP Status Distribution
description: Count how many times each HTTP status code appears in access.log, sorted descending.
hint: awk '{c[$9]++} END {for (s in c) print c[s], s}' access.log | sort -rn
solution: awk "{c[\$9]++} END {for (s in c) print c[s], s}" access.log | sort -rn

title: Department Headcount Aggregation
description: Count the number of employees in each department from employees.csv.
hint: awk -F, 'NR>1 {c[$3]++} END {for (d in c) print d, c[d]}' employees.csv
solution: awk -F, "NR>1 {c[\$3]++} END {for (d in c) print d, c[d]}" employees.csv

title: Group-by Sum per Category
description: Sum the total salary paid per city in employees.csv.
hint: awk -F, 'NR>1 {s[$5]+=$4} END {for (city in s) print city, s[city]}' employees.csv
solution: awk -F, "NR>1 {s[\$5]+=\$4} END {for (city in s) print city, s[city]}" employees.csv

title: Compound Conditional Filtering
description: Print employees earning more than 5000 from employees.csv (name and salary).

title: Log Level Counter
description: Count occurrences of each log level (INFO, WARN, ERROR) in app.log in one command.
hint: awk '{c[$3]++} END {for (l in c) print l, c[l]}' app.log
solution: awk "{c[\$3]++} END {for (l in c) print l, c[l]}" app.log

title: Print Final Column Using $NF
description: Print the last field of each access.log line (the byte count) using $NF.

title: Filter by Numeric Threshold
description: Show requests in access.log larger than 4000 bytes with their IP and size.

title: Formatted Columnar Report with printf
description: Format a clean report for 500 errors showing IP in 16-character column and status code.

title: Compute Running Maximum
description: Find the single largest response size (max bytes) in access.log.

title: Full Summary Report with Error Percentage
description: Build a mini log summary from app.log reporting total lines, error count, and error rate percentage.
hint: awk '/ERROR/{e++} {t++} END {printf "Total:%d Errors:%d Rate:%.1f%%\n", t, e, e/t*100}' app.log
solution: awk "/ERROR/{e++} {t++} END {printf \"Total:%d Errors:%d Rate:%.1f%%\\n\", t, e, e/t*100}" app.log

title: Top 3 Talker IPs Pipeline
description: Extract IPs with grep and pipe through sort, uniq, and head to display the top 3 requesting IPs.
hint: grep -oE '^[0-9.]+' access.log | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -3
solution: grep -oE "^[0-9.]+" access.log | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -3

title: Deduplicate Error IPs
description: Find all unique IPs that caused a 500 status code in access.log.

title: Attacker Identification Pipeline
description: Find the IP causing the most 403 or 404 responses and rank probe counts.

title: Clean and Mutate Configuration Pipeline
description: Filter comments/blank lines with grep, then change log_level info to log_level debug with sed in one pipe.

title: Total Bytes per Status Code
description: Report total bytes served per HTTP status code in access.log, sorted descending by bytes.
hint: awk '{bytes[$9] += $10} END {for (s in bytes) print s, bytes[s]}' access.log | sort -rn
solution: awk "{bytes[\$9] += \$10} END {for (s in bytes) print s, bytes[s]}" access.log | sort -rn

title: Compile & Test Syscall File Copier
description: Compile 01_copy_file.c and verify copying employees.csv to /tmp/copy_test.csv using open/read/write syscalls.

title: Process Lifecycle Tree Execution
description: Compile and execute 02_process_tree.c to verify fork, execvp, and waitpid parent-child status synchronization.

title: POSIX Multithreaded Work Queue
description: Compile and run 04_thread_pool.c with -pthread to verify concurrent task execution across 4 worker threads.
must_contain: All workers joined cleanly. Thread pool destroyed successfully.

title: Anonymous Pipe Stream IPC
description: Compile and run 05_pipe_ipc.c to test unidirectional kernel pipe buffer IPC between parent and child.

title: POSIX Shared Memory with Semaphores
description: Compile and run 06_shm_posix.c using -lrt to verify synchronized shared memory mutation.

title: Zero-Copy Memory-Mapped File Scanner
description: Compile and run 09_mmap_file_indexer.c on employees.csv to scan memory without user-space read buffers.

title: LKM Character Driver Simulator Run
description: Run the kernel subsystem simulator to test char_dev.c file_operations lifecycle (open, write, read, release).
must_contain: K-HARNESS VERDICT: PASS! Driver file_operations verified cleanly.

title: Kernel Memory & Buffer Transfer Check
description: Verify user-kernel memory boundaries copy_to_user and copy_from_user via the simulated kernel harness.
